speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific nature of your neck and arm pain, and does the weakness or tingling radiate down to your fingers? Please also mention if any specific movements, like looking up or turning your head, worsen these symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or tingling affect all fingers equally, or is it more prominent in the thumb, index, and middle fingers? Have you noticed any loss of grip strength or difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes, I need to rule out lower motor neuron disease. REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG/NCS is normal, this points away from peripheral nerve or lower motor neuron pathology. Let me examine your neck; do you have any tenderness over the cervical spine, and does moving your neck reproduce the arm pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sexual history is highly relevant given your symptoms, so I need to rule out neurosyphilis. REQUEST TEST: RPR and VDRL.

speaker: Doctor
text: With syphilis and peripheral neuropathies ruled out, I suspect a central nervous system issue like cervical myelopathy or ALS. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of a cervical syrinx explain your symptoms of burning pain, weakness, and absent reflexes through the mechanism of syringomyelia. This condition often results from prior trauma or obstruction of CSF flow, which aligns with your history of a motor vehicle accident. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
